content.value: The click-feedback loop that turns an accepted Did You Mean into a permanent, learned correction applied to both search engines.
The Auto Correction Loop is how Search learns from its users instead of from a hand-curated dictionary. Its canonical example: it learns
1. A user types a misspelled query and is shown a Did You Mean suggestion. 2. Clicking the suggestion writes a click-feedback event into Search Intelligence (
). 3. When the same correction is accepted across
, the loop promotes a Synonyms row —
, so the fix lands no matter which engine runs.

Requiring two *distinct* sessions filters out one-off fat-fingers and a single user's idiosyncrasy. A correction has to be independently confirmed before it becomes ground truth, which keeps the learned Synonyms table trustworthy.
Because expansion happens in the QueryPipeline upstream of dispatch, the learned correction reaches

over the Search Vector) and the Indx Engine (and its BM25F ranking) identically — a single rewrite, two engines served. The relevance lift from accumulated corrections is one of the things the Golden Eval harness measures over time.
